⭐️ Michael Saylor says Strategy and Strive can grow together 

🌐 Michael Saylor has argued that Strategy and Strive can compete for investor capital while helping each other expand the market for Bitcoin-backed preferred securities. Under Saylor’s terminology, Bitcoin represents “Digital Capital,” preferred securities such as Strategy’s STRC and Strive’s SATA represent “Digital Credit,” while MSTR and ASST sit in what he calls the “Digital Equity” category. The labels form part of Saylor’s own framework and are not formal regulatory asset classes.

📣 A 0.1% allocation from either pool would equal roughly $160 billion. Michael Saylor used that comparison to argue that Bitcoin treasury companies are competing mainly against much larger traditional equity and fixed-income markets, not only against one another. He wrote that Strategy and Strive may compete for the same individual investment, but a new investor learning how to assess one Bitcoin-linked preferred security could become more comfortable evaluating another. Saylor said several credible issuers could bring more research, trading liquidity and institutional attention to the category.

⚠️ The two companies remain separate businesses with different securities, liabilities and management decisions. Strategy issues STRC, while Strive issues SATA. Both are perpetual preferred securities, but their terms and dividend schedules differ. Strive said the purchase extended its SATA dividend reserve to 18 months, consisting at the time of 12 months of cash and another six months represented by STRC at prevailing market prices. The company described STRC as part of its reserve strategy, while stressing that market values can change.

🌍 No US vessels in Persian Gulf, Hormuz, or northern Indian Ocean: IRGC adviser

📌 Tehran, IRNA - A senior IRGC adviser says that for the first time, no US vessels are present in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman, or even the northern Indian Ocean.

Brigadier General Ali Fadavi, head of the advisory group to the commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), said in a televised interview that the Strait of Hormuz has been firmly under Iran’s control in recent months.
​
He noted that the Americans have maintained a presence in the Persian Gulf since 1853, but that for the first time, no US vessels are present in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman, or the northern Indian Ocean.
​
“The Americans have fled and moved more than a thousand kilometers away from our borders,” Fadavi said. “This did not happen by their own choice, but is the result of the authority of the Islamic Republic of Iran and the IRGC Navy.”
​
He said the Americans claim they can move a maximum of three to four million barrels of oil per day through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz, outside the area Iran has officially designated, a figure he described as insignificant compared with the volume of oil that normally passes through the strait.
​
He said that previously, more than 20 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz daily through official channels, with additional volumes exported informally.
​
The IRGC official said 46 percent of global oil exports passed through the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the 20 percent figure often cited refers to global oil consumption, since many countries consume their own production rather than exporting it.
​
He said oil exports through the route are now facing major disruption, which has had a broad impact on the global economy, including the United States and Europe.
​
He warned that any further escalation in the region would harm the United States, saying American warships are directly threatened by IRGC naval forces in the Strait of Hormoz.
​
The adviser said the United States would be forced to rely on its vessels to escalate tensions. “Even if they bomb a region every day, they cannot impose their demands as long as they lack a physical presence.”
​
Fadavi added that US vessels are “exposed and vulnerable” to the IRGC Navy. According to him, US forces have repeatedly attempted to bring their warships into the Strait of Hormuz but were attacked by the IRGC Navy and Aerospace Force.
​
“Any escalation of tensions will definitely be to their own detriment,” Fadavi said.

📲 @Irna_en​

Turkmenistan has introduced electronic visas. Invitation for tourists is no longer required

The State Migration Service launched the system on October 1, 2026. The portal is evisa.migration.gov.tm. The basis for this was amendments to the "Migration Law" signed in April 2025. It took one and a half years from the law to the launch of the system.

Previously, a tourist almost never applied by himself. A letter from a licensed local company was required, which had to be approved by the migration service before going to the consulate or obtaining a visa on arrival. This step is removed for the tourist electronic visa.

There are three categories on the portal.
e-TU, tourism. There is no invitation required among the mandatory documents. The itinerary, hotel reservation, and medical insurance are listed as optional. The portal does not publish the duration of stay.

e-BS, business, max 30 days. An invitation from a company or organization registered in Turkmenistan, indicating the applicant's position, is required.

e-HM, humanitarian. An official letter from a humanitarian organization or UN agency regarding the assignment is required.

Common package for all three categories: a scan of the passport page with a photo, a passport valid for at least 6 months on the date of entry, a recent color photo on a white background following the ICAO standard, a work email. The visa will be sent to this address.

Processing times: regular procedure 7 business days, expedited 3 days, "super expedited" 24 hours. The fee is calculated in the application, paid online in dollars with bank commission on top. There is no visible price list.

What the portal does not mention. The list of passports eligible for a visa. Entry points where the electronic visa is accepted: Ashgabat airport, land, sea. The duration of the tourist visa. The website was barely accessible on the launch day.

The old procedure with invitation is still valid for applications that travel agencies have already submitted before October 1. Some operators still process electronic visas only along with a full tour: biometrics and payments are made by the client, while handling is done by the agency.

The country has not become visa-free. The obligatory intermediary for the tourist, who now applies independently, has been removed. Business and humanitarian visas still start with an internal letter. As there is no list of countries and duration of stay yet, an independent trip remains an application, not a ticket.
